name: FxPro
lead: The only broker in our comparison where the counterparty company's name can't be found on the registration screen at all. It's there — but only inside the PDF client agreement.

processes.label: Registration
needed: A couple of minutes for the form — plus 2 extra clicks if you want to see the legal entity

items.caption: Fill in country, email, and password.
items.note: Country is detected automatically by IP and inserted into the form's URL — that's how FxPro picks which group entity becomes your counterparty. For example, the .../register/md/crc route leads to the Costa Rica entity (crc = Costa Rica Markets Ltd).

items.caption: On the next screen, enter your name, date of birth, and phone number.
items.note: The phone country code is filled in based on the country you selected earlier.

blocks.title: The legal entity isn't named on the registration form
blocks.body: The only line at the bottom of the form reads "FxPro is a registered trademark utilised under an approved licensing agreement." No company, no jurisdiction, no licence number.

items.caption: To find out who you're actually signing the contract with, open the "Terms and conditions" link on the form → Legal Documentation section.
Open the "Client Agreement". Right in the file name you can see: "Costa Rica Markets Ltd — June 2026 New entity...".

blocks.register_note: The FxPro brand does have regulators — the FCA (UK), the Bahamas Securities Commission, the Seychelles FSA (fxpro.com/about/licences). But all of them license OTHER entities in the group. Costa Rica Markets Ltd, which is the entity clients from most CIS and European countries actually sign a contract with, isn't mentioned under any of these regulators, and the contract itself contains no reference to any regulatory body at all.
blocks.quote: «FxPro is the brand and trading name of Costa Rica Markets Ltd. which is a private limited company incorporated in Costa Rica.» (клиентский договор, п. 1.2)
blocks.confirm_note: The registration screen itself doesn't name the entity at all — only the trademark line. You can only find out the real counterparty by opening the PDF agreement, two clicks deep into the documentation, which a regular user isn't required to go through during registration.
missing: a regulator and licence for THIS entity — even though the FxPro brand overall does have regulators (see above), just not for this one
a compensation fund — FSCS protection belongs to the UK entity, FxPro UK Limited, not to the Costa Rica entity that actually serves most clients from the CIS and Europe
a published percentage of losing accounts — not published on any page

items.caption: Right after registration, a "You are Ready to Start!" screen appears with a QR code for the mobile app.
items.note: If you don't need the app, click "Proceed with web".

items.caption: You land on "Wallet & Accounts": a separate wallet (for moving money between accounts) and a trading account — already created, under the "Real account" tab.

blocks.title: What to notice
blocks.body: The account FxPro creates by default is labelled "Real", not "Demo" — even though the balance is zero and you can't trade until it's funded. If you want to practise without money, switch to the "Demo accounts" tab and create a demo account separately — it isn't selected by default.

rows: FxPro WebTrader, MT4, MT5, cTrader, TradingView, mobile app
Standard — none; Raw+ and Elite — 3.5 USD per lot one-way on major pairs and gold; cTrader — 35 USD per 1,000,000 turnover

items.caption: In the sidebar, open "Deposit", pick a method, and enter an amount.
items.note: Methods: card (Visa/Mastercard), Binance Pay, USDT, BTC, Ethereum, other crypto, Skrill, Neteller, bank transfer.

blocks.title: What to notice
blocks.body: 0% is the fee charged by the FxPro platform itself. It doesn't cancel out your own bank's or payment provider's fees (especially for cards not denominated in USD) — check with your card issuer separately.

processes.label: Verification
processes.intro: Without verification the account is created and visible in the dashboard, but documents will still be requested before your first withdrawal.

items.caption: Open the profile menu (icon in the top right corner) → "Settings".
On the "Your documents" tab — status "Identity Verification: Not uploaded". Click "Upload" to attach a document.
There's a separate "Optional documents" block — this is where you upload whatever the platform has asked for beyond standard verification.
items.note: The dropdown is a list of document-type options, not a ready-made requirements list: Debit/credit card copy, Bank statement, FxPro Internal Form, KYC Request, Accounting Request, Other. Pick whichever matches FxPro's specific request.

items.caption: MT5 WebTrader opens: an instrument list with the current spread on the left, a chart on the right, and open positions at the bottom.

blocks.title: Why we don't publish FxPro's spread as a single number
body: We have three independent measurements of the same EUR/USD, and all three disagree: the live quote on the site's public page — about 1.4 pips; in the same terminal's favourites list — 0.2; in the terminal's full instrument search (below) — 0.1.

A partial explanation turned up right on the instrument page: "Note: Price data indicated above may be delayed by 15 minutes." But a fifteen-minute delay doesn't explain a sevenfold difference between the site and the terminal, so the question isn't fully resolved.

As long as the reason is unknown, "FxPro's spread" doesn't have a single defined value, and we'd rather say that directly than pick whichever number looks best. Only a measurement on a real account, at the actual moment of a trade, resolves it.

items.caption: To see the spread for any instrument at once, open search (the magnifying glass icon at the top) — a table appears with every pair and a live spread in the middle column.

blocks.caption: Terminal snapshot, 2026-08-07, outside the methodology windows — shown as a reference point, not a rules-compliant measurement.

This is what FxPro officially publishes — on the instrument page, not as a summary table (it doesn't have one). Swap was collected only for EUR/USD; the other eleven instruments follow the same URL pattern.

items.caption: To place a trade, click an instrument in the list — a ticket opens with Market / Limit / Stop tabs.
items.note: Market — at the current price; Limit — triggers once the price reaches your level; Stop — the opposite of Limit, for entering on a breakout.

items.caption: Enter the volume, and if you want, set Stop Loss and Take Profit — both optional, but without a Stop Loss the trade has no limit on losses.

blocks.title: What to notice
blocks.body: "Margin required" under the ticket isn't a fee — it's the amount locked in your account against the open position. It's released when the trade closes, but while the position is open, you can't use it.

blocks.title: Price alerts — without an open position
blocks.body: In the terminal you can set a price alert (the bell icon) — you'll get a notification once the instrument reaches the level you want, without having to keep a trade open or watch the chart.
